summary: Updates RFC 5761 by clarifying how SDP offer/answer works for multiplexing RTP and RTCP on one port. An answerer may include the a=rtcp-mux attribute only if the offer contained it.

plainLanguage.summary: Two people agree on one shared phone line for both talking and notes. This rule says you can only agree to share if the other person suggested it first.

questions: can an sdp answer add rtcp-mux
how does rtp rtcp multiplexing negotiation work
what does rfc 8035 change in rfc 5761
subtitle: A one-rule fix: an answer may only ask for RTP/RTCP multiplexing if the offer did.

tldr.problem: RFC 5761 lets two endpoints share one port for RTP and RTCP, negotiated with the a=rtcp-mux attribute, but its text was unclear on whether an answerer could add the attribute when the offer did not contain it.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8035 replaces the relevant text in Section 5.1.1 of RFC 5761: the answerer can include a=rtcp-mux only if the offer contained it, and the outcome applies to both directions.
tldr.outcome: Both sides now follow the same rule, so they cannot end up disagreeing about where RTCP packets go. The RFC updates RFC 5761 and is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 8035 is a Proposed Standard published in November 2016. It updates RFC 5761, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Ambiguity Being Fixed
sections.content:
RFC 5761 describes how to multiplex RTP data packets and RTP Control Protocol (RTCP) packets on a single UDP port. It also describes how to negotiate that multiplexing with the SDP offer/answer mechanism from RFC 3264, using an a=rtcp-mux attribute.

The gap was narrow. The text was unclear on whether an answerer is allowed to include the attribute in an answer even if the offer did not contain it. This document closes that gap and also clarifies that the negotiation applies in both directions.
sections.plainLanguage: Two people are deciding how to share one phone line. Nobody had written down whether the second person could suggest sharing first. Now it is written down.

sections.title: The Core Rule
sections.content:
The update covers two points. First, an answerer can include an a=rtcp-mux attribute in an answer only if the associated offer contained the attribute. Second, the negotiation of RTP and RTCP multiplexing is for usage in both directions.

The change is made as an OLD TEXT / NEW TEXT replacement of Section 5.1.1 of RFC 5761. Nothing else in RFC 5761 is changed by this document.
sections.plainLanguage: You can only say "yes, let us share" if the other person asked to share. And when you agree, both of you share, not just one.

sections.title: How the Offer and Answer Behave
sections.content:
If the offerer wants to multiplex, the initial offer MUST include the attribute at the media level. If the offer contains a=rtcp-mux and the answerer wants to multiplex too, the answer MUST include a media-level a=rtcp-mux, and the RTP payload types in the answer MUST conform to the rules in Section 4 of RFC 5761.

If the offer does not contain the attribute, the answerer MUST NOT include it in the answer, and MUST NOT multiplex RTP and RTCP on a single port.

  • If the answer contains a=rtcp-mux, the offerer and the answerer MUST multiplex RTP and RTCP on a single port.
  • If the answer does not contain it, they MUST NOT multiplex. They should send and receive RTCP on a port chosen by the usual port-selection rules: either the port pair, or a signalled port if the a=rtcp: attribute is also included. This happens when talking to a peer that does not understand a=rtcp-mux.
sections.plainLanguage: If you were not asked to share, you cannot start sharing. If you were asked and you say yes, you both share. If you say nothing, you both keep separate lines.

sections.title: The Example Offer
sections.content:
The RFC keeps the example offer from RFC 5761. It carries one audio stream, m=audio 49170 RTP/AVP 97, with a=rtpmap:97 iLBC/8000 and a=rtcp-mux, sent from IPv6 address 2001:DB8::211:24ff:fea3:7a2e.

The text describes it as a unicast voice-over-IP session using the RTP/AVP profile with Internet Low Bit Rate Codec (iLBC) coding. The answerer is requested to send both RTP and RTCP to port 49170 on that address.

The new text also covers declarative use of SDP. There, the presence of a=rtcp-mux signals that the sender will multiplex RTP and RTCP on the same port. The receiver MUST be prepared to receive RTCP on the RTP port, and any resource reservation needs to include the RTCP bandwidth.
sections.plainLanguage: The example is like a note saying "call me on line 49170, and I will use that one line for talking and for notes."

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The security considerations for RTP and RTCP multiplexing are described in RFC 5761, and this specification does not impact them.

For IANA, a reference to this document has been added to the att-field (media level only) registration rtcp-mux in the "Session Description Protocol (SDP) Parameters" registry.
sections.plainLanguage: Because only a rule about who may say yes was clarified, nothing new is risky. The official list just got a note pointing to this new rule.
